cause_quote: The new transfer path runs `fsSync.unlinkSync(options.sourcePath)` before `if (!sameFileStatFingerprint(moved.identity, identity))`, so it compares the receipt against a birth time that can change when the original hard-link name is removed.
user_saw: On affected Linux hosts, `openclaw doctor --fix` failed to save its required pre-migration SQLite backup and reported that the staging file changed during transfer.
summary: The fix limits the staging fingerprint to device, inode, and size while retaining separate checks of the snapshot bytes.
reasoning: The parent of #162403 already had Doctor call `createVerifiedSqliteSnapshot`, which copied the private image into publication staging and took a fresh stat after unlinking the final staging name. #162403 added an earlier hard-link transfer to that existing path and applied the birth-time comparison across an unlink. The fix PR reproduced the resulting failure when Node/libuv reported ctime as birth time even though the inode, size, and bytes stayed unchanged.
